name: UT-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Kennedy running with large financial advantage
Democratic challenger raised only ~$54k with minimal cash
Prediction markets price Republican win at ~94%
model.rationale: The district's R+17 lean, Kennedy's incumbency and roughly 18-to-1 fundraising edge over Jonny Larsen, and markets pricing a Republican win near 94% all point the same direction, with no polls or ratings suggesting movement. The forecast stays at the fundamentals-implied margin of about 17 points Republican.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Larsen within single digits, or major outside spending entering the race, would warrant a shift toward Lean R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's 4th District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about 17 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Mike Kennedy is running for reelection and holds a commanding financial position, having raised roughly $970,000 with nearly $390,000 on hand. Democratic challenger Jonny Larsen has raised about $54,000 and reports little cash remaining, with no outside spending on either side.

Independent and Libertarian candidates are on the ballot but show minimal resources. Prediction markets give the Republican roughly a 94% chance of winning. With no public polling or expert ratings available, the race rests on district fundamentals, which strongly favor the incumbent party. The expected margin is about 17 points Republican, consistent with a Safe R rating, though the absence of polling leaves moderate uncertainty around that estimate.
